Using social network data from 9th and 10th-grade students (N = 247) across three schools on a Northern Plains reservation, we employed exponential random graph models (ERGMs) to analyze factors shaping friendship ties.

Trained research team members administered the survey during school hours. Students provided responses directly on tablets. Written informed assent was obtained digitally from all participants, with hard copies provided afterward. For students under 18, passive parental permission procedures were utilized.

The survey consisted of two primary sections: the first collected demographic information, measures of AI identity, depression, and substance use; the second collected directed friendship nominations.
Students were asked to "select up to 10 friends you are closest with in grades 7th-12th at your school."

For these cases, we utilized available peer perception data to infer behavior. Participants were asked to nominate up to 10 closest friends and then answer questions about each nominated peer’s behavior, including: ‘In the past year, how often has this person drunk alcohol (more than a sip)?’
